numerical_failure.observed_behavior: Angle.to_string carried/rounded seconds into higher fields at the half-unit boundary too early or performed double rounding when fields=1, producing incorrect sexagesimal components (minutes/degrees) from the input seconds.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: Carry/round seconds into the next minute/field only when appropriate per correct rounding on ties, and avoid rounding the seconds into minutes before rounding minutes into degrees when fields=1 (i.e., no double rounding).
trigger_conditions: Angle.to_string(precision=0) with an input where seconds are 59.49999s in the d/m/s string representation; the seconds carry into the next minute half a unit too early
Angle.to_string(fields=1) with an input where fields=1 causes seconds to be rounded into minutes before minutes are rounded into degrees (double rounding)
Internally: fields==3 (seconds component) uses built-in round instead of NumPy round to handle ties consistently, and fields==1 should not round seconds into minutes before minutes into degrees
oracle_clues: Fixed two rounding errors in Angle.to_string. The seconds were carried into the next minute half a unit too early, so e.g. Angle("1d2m59.49999s").to_string(precision=0) gave 1d03m00s instead of 1d02m59s.
With fields=1 the seconds were rounded into the minutes before the minutes were rounded into the degrees, rounding twice, so e.g. Angle("285d29m41.76s").to_string(fields=1) gave 286d instead of 285d.

category_specific_evidence: Violation of the tie/rounding rule used to decide whether seconds at exactly “half a unit in the last digit shown” should carry into minutes/degrees: code comment says builtin round is used because “NumPy's disagrees with the formatting on ties”, and rounding is implemented via `round(float(values[2]), ndp) >= 60.0` when `fields == 3` (with `ndp = 8 if precision is None else precision`).

When `fields==3`, carry into the next minute should occur only at or above the half-unit threshold, not when below it: examples in tests show no carry just below half a unit and carry at/above it: `Angle("1d2m59.49999s", precision=0) -> "1d02m59s"` vs `Angle("1d2m59.5s", precision=0) -> "1d03m00s"`; similarly `precision=1`: `"1d2m59.94s" -> "1d02m59.9s"` vs `"1d2m59.96s" -> "1d03m00.0s"`; and `precision=2`: `"1d2m59.994s" -> "1d02m59.99s"` vs carry implied at/above half-unit.

When `fields<2`/`fields==1`, seconds must not be rounded into minutes before minutes are rounded into degrees, because that would “round twice”: documented bugfix examples show `Angle("285d29m41.76s").to_string(fields=1) -> "285d"` (no carry/ no double-round) while the bug caused `"286d"` instead.
reproduction_risks: Reproduction may depend on whether Python’s builtin `round` or NumPy’s rounding is used for tie-handling, since the patch notes they disagree on ties.

Reproduction may depend on the `fields` parameter path (`fields==3`, `fields==2`, `fields==1`) because different rounding/carry logic applies, including avoiding “round twice” behavior when seconds would otherwise be rounded into minutes prematurely.
Reproduction may depend on how `precision` is interpreted to determine the last displayed digit (`ndp = 8 if precision is None else precision`).
